subject: host-effect-authorization.v10
protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; did not author v1-v10; successor to v9 (Codex REJECT at HAE9-CX-01, frozen b28cab51...)
summary: The hygiene layer of v10 is clean and every recited fact replicates: all five prompt pins reproduce, all 30 measurable recordedInputs digests reproduce, the D-032 section extraction rule still resolves to lines 1621-1654 hashing 00085513... at the LIVE COORD (7d396ca7...), and every self-recited count (19 closed members, 19 mapping destinations, 15 scope members, 4 covered acts, 4 CA-3 subtypes, 3 outcome members) is exact. No prohibited act is present. The repair itself does not survive. HAE9-CX-01 was that classPredicateDomain.rule quantified over every when/nullWhen/requiredWhen predicate in the scope shape while policyProvenance.nullWhen keys on a consent-carrier literal. v10 narrows the rule to actionClass-discriminator predicates and adds a consentCarrierPredicateDomain block. That answers the finding nominally but not structurally, and it opens two new holes on the same axis. First, consentCarrier is not a member of consentRecordsScopeShape (15 members, closed, additionalMembers forbidden) and is not a member of doctor v4's consentRecords[] (13 members, measured from its own bytes); the artifact's only destination for it is prose in residualLimitation, which the artifact's own honesty rules forbid as a carrier. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE, the fixture cited as the repair's evidence, therefore keys its four parentRecords on a discriminator that does not exist in the object being validated - unlike its sibling FC-BOUND-SHAPE, whose parentRecords key on actionClass, a real consentRecords[] member. Second, v10 newly minted policyProvenance.requiredWhen ('pre-existing-policy'), which v9 did not have; the narrowed classPredicateDomain.rule no longer reaches it and consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo names only nullWhen, so the artifact's newest predicate is governed by no declared domain. The repair reproduces the defect class it was written to close.

findings.title: The repaired predicate's discriminator has no structured carrier, so FC-CARRIER-SHAPE cannot be claimed to pass
findings.whatTheArtifactClaims: consentCarrierPredicateDomain.rule: 'policyProvenance.nullWhen is a consentCarrier-domain predicate, not an actionClass predicate. It is null exactly when consentCarrier is invocation-time-naming. It is required/non-null when consentCarrier is pre-existing-policy. Source/join: doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.consentCarrier (disclosed in residualLimitation) and doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.policyProvenance'. authorityClaim and honestyRepairsFromV9 both cite FC-CARRIER-SHAPE covering both carrier branches as the repair evidence.
whatIMeasured: consentRecordsScopeShape.members is exactly 15 names: actor, actionSubtype, invocation, checks, resources, targetIdentity, observationDeadline, byteCap, endpointSet, platform, policyProvenance, designContractRef, productAdmissionRefs, owners, auditIdentity. consentCarrier is not among them. topLevelMemberCount 15 agrees.

consentRecordsScopeShape.closed is true and additionalMembers is 'forbidden. Additive members require a successor of this contract and a doctor successor that accepts them.' So consentCarrier cannot lawfully be added to the object at validation time.

doctor-contract.v4.json consentModel.mandatoryPostReport.recordMembers, read from its own bytes at df2e7175..., is exactly 13 members: id, actionClass, permissionRef, scope, endpoint, bytes, authorization, execution, result, residualLimitation, effectOutcome, enforcementDisclosure, argumentVector. There is no consentCarrier member anywhere on the consent record.

The artifact's sole destination for the member is doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.consentCarrier = 'disclosed in residualLimitation as the carrier, never as authorization'. residualLimitation is doctor v4's free-text member.

consentCarrier occurs 13 times in v10. Setting aside authorityClaim, honestyRepairsFromV9 and the domain block's own self-reference, every occurrence is either the authorizationRecord-side closed member (line 198), the prose destination (line 270), or an FC-CARRIER-SHAPE parentRecords key (lines 929, 934, 939, 944). None places it in the serialized scope.
findings.whyItIsABlocker: FC-CARRIER-SHAPE's passProperty requires a validator to distinguish four parent records, two of which must REFUSE: invocation-time-naming with policyProvenance present, and pre-existing-policy with policyProvenance null. Deciding either requires reading consentCarrier. A validator handed a consentRecords[].scope cannot read it: it is not in the closed 15-member object, it is not elsewhere on the 13-member consent record, and the artifact routes it to free text. The fixture is therefore not constructible as specified. The asymmetry with its own sibling is exact and is the cleanest demonstration: FC-BOUND-SHAPE's parentRecords key on actionClass, which IS a real consentRecords[] member, which is why that fixture is decidable and why it could carry the unmatchedSerializedClass totality property. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE keys on a discriminator with no structured existence and carries no analogous totality clause.
artifactContradictsItselfAt: outcomeVocabulary.serialization.normativeBinding: 'Prose in residualLimitation is not a substitute.'
effectCommit.processDeath: INDETERMINATE must be at effectOutcome, 'Never narrated only in residualLimitation.'
acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses.FC-ROUND-TRIP requires a distinct auditIdentity handle to 'appear here, not only in prose.'

doctor-contract.v4 applies the same standard against itself, closing off the free-text result member as a carrier because 'narrating an unknown outcome in prose is the narration the corpus's honesty discipline exists to stop.'
findings.note: The artifact holds prose-is-not-a-carrier against effectOutcome, auditIdentity and residual narration, then rests its newest predicate and its newest fixture on a prose-only discriminator. Either consentCarrier becomes a closed member of consentRecordsScopeShape (which the artifact's own additionalMembers rule says requires a successor contract and a doctor successor that accepts it), or the carrier predicate cannot be stated as a machine-checkable property of the scope and FC-CARRIER-SHAPE must be re-scoped to the authorizationRecord side, where consentCarrier does exist as a closed member with closed values.
findings.notRepairableByPrompt: PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT does not reach this. Nothing moved; this is an internal structural defect in the subject's own bytes.

findings.title: v10 mints a new predicate that the narrowed rule no longer reaches and the new domain does not enumerate, leaving it governed by nothing
whatIMeasured: v9's policyProvenance member had exactly four keys: name, type, nullable, nullWhen. It had NO requiredWhen. Verified by structural flattening diff of v9 (a3857210...) against v10 (5a0b84e3...).

v10 ADDS four keys to that member: nullWhenDomain 'consentCarrier', requiredWhen 'pre-existing-policy', closedValuesWhenPresent true, and sourceJoin. requiredWhen is a predicate that did not exist in v9.

classPredicateDomain.rule in v9: 'Every when / nullWhen / requiredWhen predicate in this scope shape uses only these four literals.' In v10: 'Every when / nullWhen / requiredWhen predicate whose discriminator is consentRecords[].actionClass uses only these four literals... This rule does not quantify over consentCarrier-domain predicates.'
consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo is a one-element array: ['consentRecordsScopeShape.members[policyProvenance].nullWhen']. requiredWhen is not listed.
The member carries nullWhenDomain but no requiredWhenDomain. The domain annotation was applied to one predicate and not to the sibling predicate added in the same edit.
findings.whyItIsABlocker: After the narrowing, a predicate is governed only if some domain block claims it. classPredicateDomain expressly disclaims consentCarrier-domain predicates, so it does not reach requiredWhen. consentCarrierPredicateDomain reaches exactly what appliesTo enumerates, and it enumerates only nullWhen. The newly minted requiredWhen therefore falls between the two blocks. This is the same shape as HAE9-CX-01 - a scope-shape predicate whose governing domain is wrong or absent - reintroduced by the repair for that finding, in the same member, in the same edit. v9 was over-inclusive and wrong; v10 is under-inclusive and silent, which is worse for a fail-closed artifact because an ungoverned predicate raises no contradiction to trip on.
findings.mitigationConsidered: consentCarrierPredicateDomain.rule's body does state the semantics: 'It is required/non-null when consentCarrier is pre-existing-policy.' I weighed that as possibly sufficient and rejected it. This artifact treats enumerations as normative and closed throughout - closedMemberCount, mappedMemberCount, topLevelMemberCount, closedValues, closedItemShape, and classPredicateDomain's own unmatchedSerializedClass totality clause. appliesTo is this block's scope enumeration and it is under-inclusive. A checker walking appliesTo, which is the only machine-followable artifact here, misses the predicate. Prose in a rule body restating a semantic is exactly the substitute the artifact refuses everywhere else.
findings.alsoMissing: consentCarrierPredicateDomain has no totality clause analogous to classPredicateDomain.unmatchedSerializedClass. classPredicateDomain closes the loop with 'every legal serialized class must select exactly one byteCap variant and the matching targetIdentity / endpointSet requiredness'. The carrier domain declares two closed values and asserts no corresponding exhaustiveness property over them.

findings.title: closedValuesWhenPresent is asserted as boolean true, naming no closed set, and defeats the mapping's own totality rule
whatIMeasured: The key closedValuesWhenPresent appears exactly twice in v10. At members[1] (actionSubtype) it carries an array of nine literals: SPAWN, IN_PROCESS, OUT_OF_ROOT_READ, LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE, KEYCHAIN, PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY, PATH-TRUST-STATE-REFRESH, PATH-INDEX-REACH, PATH-DECLARED-EXTERNAL-SERVICE. At members[10] (policyProvenance) the same key carries the boolean true.
No closed value set for policyProvenance exists anywhere in v10.
authorizationRecord.closedMembers policyProvenance.semantics reads 'For pre-existing-policy: the exact policy source identity' - an open-ended identity, not an enumerable set.
This key is new in v10; v9's policyProvenance member did not carry it.
findings.whyItMatters: doctorV4FieldMapping.rule requires the mapping be 'Total over the 19 authorizationRecord closed members AND over every legal value of those members', and states 'A legal variant with no destination is a defect.' Discharging that for policyProvenance requires enumerating its legal values. If closedValuesWhenPresent is true, the closed set is normative and unnamed, so the enumeration cannot be performed and the totality rule cannot be discharged for this member. If the values are in fact open, as the member's own semantics say, then the key asserts something false. Both readings are defects, and the same key means an enumerated list eleven members earlier in the same array, so the type inconsistency is internal to one object.
findings.suggestedDirection: Either name the closed set, or drop the key and let the member stand as the open exact-source-identity string its semantics already describe.

The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md whole-file pin supports only the D-032 section named at governingDecisions.D-032.selector / sectionSha256. doctor v4, permission v1, and the join review are pinned as environment and as predecessor inputs, not as applied authority. Append-only COORD after this remasurement... Does not SATISFY DR-105 or DR-114.' v10 deletes the second, third and fourth sentences and keeps the rest.

findings.whyItMatters: The deleted sentence - 'The COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md whole-file pin supports only the D-032 section named at governingDecisions.D-032.selector / sectionSha256' - was precisely what made a stale whole-file COORD pin lawful in an artifact that also records the live one. v9 stated that reconciliation; v10 removes it and leaves both pins standing with nothing explaining the divergence. The deleted companion sentence, 'doctor v4, permission v1, and the join review are pinned as environment and as predecessor inputs, not as applied authority', was the remeasurement-side anchor for whatThisDoesNotDo[0]. Neither deletion appears in honestyRepairsFromV9. In a corpus whose discipline is that recited facts must replicate and that a change be declared where it is made, a change record that names one repair while the bytes carry four independent edits is itself a defect.
findings.explicitlyNotABlocker: I verified the underlying fact is sound, so this is a record-keeping and reconciliation defect rather than a false statement. The D-032 section extraction rule DOES still reproduce at the live COORD: lines 1621-1654 of COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 7d396ca7... hash to 00085513a0551aded3b1996bf448c42f16265ce0a4409eb5d926108d1bd63367, matching sectionSha256 exactly, with the first line the D-032 heading and the last line the terminating horizontal rule as sectionExtractionRule requires. COORD moved append-only, so the line range is stable. PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT covers COORD having moved; it does not license deleting the artifact's own scoping sentence or under-reporting the delta.

predecessorFindingVerification.HAE9-CX-01: NOT REPAIRED. Recorded as REPAIRED at honestyRepairsFromV9[0]; I do not concur. I did not read the frozen Codex v9 verdict (b28cab51...) and confirmed the underlying v9 defect from v9's own bytes: v9's classPredicateDomain.rule read 'Every when / nullWhen / requiredWhen predicate in this scope shape uses only these four literals', while v9's policyProvenance.nullWhen read 'invocation-time-naming', which is not one of CA-1..CA-4. The finding is answered at the level of the sentence and not at the level of the shape.

verdictNote: REJECT at 2 blockers and 2 should-fix. The v10 repair is the kind that reads as complete and does not survive being checked against the shape it governs. HAE9-CX-01 named a contradiction between classPredicateDomain.rule and policyProvenance.nullWhen; v10 removes the contradiction by narrowing the rule and declaring a second domain, and both of those edits are correct in isolation. What neither edit does is give the new domain's discriminator a place to exist. consentCarrier is absent from the closed 15-member scope, absent from doctor v4's 13-member consent record, and routed by this artifact's own mapping to free text in residualLimitation - the exact carrier the artifact forbids at FC-OUTCOME, at outcomeVocabulary.normativeBinding, at effectCommit.processDeath and at FC-ROUND-TRIP, and that doctor v4 forbids against itself. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE, cited in both authorityClaim and honestyRepairsFromV9 as the evidence that both carrier branches are covered, keys four parent records on that discriminator and so cannot be built; its sibling FC-BOUND-SHAPE keys on actionClass, a real consent-record member, which is why that fixture works and carries a totality clause this one lacks. Separately, the narrowing is what lets the newly minted policyProvenance.requiredWhen escape governance entirely: classPredicateDomain expressly disclaims carrier-domain predicates and consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo names only nullWhen, so the artifact's newest predicate is claimed by neither block. That is HAE9-CX-01's own defect class, reintroduced in the same member by the edit written to close it. The hygiene layer is genuinely clean and I want that on the record: every pin, every recorded input, every recited count and the D-032 section extraction all replicate, including at the live COORD rather than only at the historical pin the artifact names, and the six fail-closed and preview-denial regions are byte-identical to v9. The defects are confined to the repair itself.
